svg.font-family: Geist, Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif
svg.title: Security
svg.desc: How ORION is kept from abusing the machine he has full access to. Nothing depends on the model behaving. A call from a place (voice, the HUD, Discord, a scheduled job, another app) passes one door, the hub, which refuses what that place may never do whatever anyone says, blocks any call whose arguments hold a secret, asks for your yes after untrusted content or where a place says to, and records everything in the activity log. What runs is boxed: commands in a bubblewrap sandbox with a clean environment, connectors with only their own secrets (those nobody reviewed in the sandbox too), the file tools away from what the sandbox hides. Every result passes the redactor before the model, the HUD, Discord, logs, memory or the activity log receives it. Secrets live in the vault (the system keyring, or private files in a container), and config.yaml holds only references. Limits only you can lift: channel limits, installs that ask you, switches that go off but never on, safety and secrets the AI can't change, answers it can't give for you, the HUD that answers this PC alone, other apps that count as untrusted, and the activity log.
svg.text: He has full access to the machine, so nothing here depends on the model behaving: every call passes one door, secrets are kept where no model can reach, and what runs is boxed.
A CALL, FROM A PLACE TO THE PC
The hub: the one door every call passes
What a place may never do is refused, and no yes lifts it:
Discord can't reach the PC's power or its commands.
A call whose arguments hold a key, a token or a password is
blocked, however it is written (base64, hex, URL-encoded).
After untrusted content, for anything that changes or sends,
and where a place asks. HUD, aloud or Discord; no answer is no.
Calls, questions and answers, refusals and blocks: the activity
log says who asked and who allowed it, with no secret in it.
The file tools can't read what the sandbox hides,
or change his code or what starts programs.
Run in a bubblewrap sandbox: the PC is read-only,
keys and sign-ins are hidden, the environment is
clean, there is no desktop. The network is open,
Each gets an environment of its own and only
its own secrets; one nobody reviewed runs in
A secret is cut out of
safety.channels what each place may never do, and what it always asks about
safety.sandbox_* what commands can write, what is hidden from them, their network
SECRETS: WHERE THEY LIVE, AND WHERE THEY ARE CUT OUT
The desktop's keyring, or private files in a
container. config.yaml keeps only a reference,
${secret:NAME}: the value is never in it.
orion secret set NAME asks for it hidden,
It knows every secret in the vault, and each as it
can be disguised (base64, hex, URL, JSON), and the
shape of 30 kinds of token: keys, JWTs, private
keys, bot tokens. One automaton: 0.14 ms for
Cut out of everything he shows or keeps
Discord, jobs and other apps each have things
they may never do, even with your yes: power,
commands, settings, the models. Only you
change them, in the HUD or config.yaml.
He adds, changes or removes a connector or a
plugin only with your yes, asked where you spoke;
never from Discord or a job. Whether one runs
in the sandbox is yours alone.
He can switch a tool or a connector off, never
back on. Only you can, in Customize. The
browser's code-running tools start switched off.
He reads safety.* but never changes it, nor
secrets, plugins, prompts, paths or tokens.
Settings show a secret as set or not set.
Every yes comes from your side (a HUD, your
voice, Discord), never from a tool call.
The HUD listens on 127.0.0.1 and checks Host
and Origin; other devices pair with a code.
No other site, no DNS rebinding, no framing.
Calls through /mcp count as app: they can't
leave the sandbox or change connectors, and
what they save goes to unverified.md.
What he did is on record
The Activity page lists each call, question,
answer, refusal and block, and who asked or
allowed it: titles and outcomes, no secret.
